## The defect

`infra/terraform/user_data.sh` asserts the mount for the GATE-SCRATCH volume but not for the
GERRIT DATA volume:

(Line numbers below are as of `25d1d683e55a`, the pre-fix `origin/main`, so they can be
checked rather than trusted.)

- gate-scratch: `mountpoint -q` at `:161`, FATALing at `:162` with "refusing to leave gate
  scratch on the ROOT filesystem" — the block is `:161-164`.
- `/var/gerrit` (the `mount_ebs_volume ... /var/gerrit` call site, `:135-138`): **no assertion
  at all.** It FATALs only on an unresolvable device, never on a mount that did not take.

Both fstab entries use `nofail`. And `mount -a` returning 0 does NOT mean the mount happened —
`nofail` skips quietly. That was PROVEN by execution in a sandbox: stubbing `mount` to return 0
without mounting is exactly the documented nofail-skip mode, and the gate-scratch path caught it
while nothing would catch it for `/var/gerrit`.

So a `/var/gerrit` mount that silently does not take leaves **Gerrit running on the root
filesystem**, with nothing raising and nothing asserting.

## Why this is the more serious instance of the class

This is the same silent-fallback-to-root failure that ADR 0112 exists to prevent — but on the
MORE valuable volume. Consequences of Gerrit running on root:

- The Gerrit repository data goes to a 60 GiB root volume rather than its dedicated 50 GiB one.
- Root disk pressure returns. Root has already hit **97%** once (2026-09-02), which took Gerrit
  fully offline for five hours.
- Backups silently cover the wrong thing: the DLM policy snapshots the DATA volume. If Gerrit is
  actually writing to root, the daily snapshots contain nothing of value, and root is not on a
  schedule at all.

The asymmetry between the two mounts looks unintentional rather than considered — the gate-scratch
assertion was added by ADR 0112's work, and the older `/var/gerrit` path simply never got one.

## IMMEDIATE RELEVANCE: a Gerrit stop/start is pending

An approved `terraform apply` will update `aws_instance.gerrit`'s `user_data` and, per provider
v5.100.0 defaults, STOP/START the instance. On restart, `mount -a` runs against the real fstab. If
`/var/gerrit` silently fails to mount, **Gerrit comes back up on the root filesystem and nothing
says so.**

Mitigation until this is fixed: after any instance stop/start, explicitly verify
`mountpoint -q /var/gerrit` (and `findmnt -no SOURCE /var/gerrit`) BEFORE declaring the host
healthy. Do not rely on Gerrit responding as evidence that its data volume is mounted — it will
respond either way.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1 - `user_data.sh` asserts `mountpoint -q /var/gerrit` after `mount -a`, and FAILS LOUDLY
      when the mount did not take, in the same shape as the gate-scratch assertion at
      `:161-164`.
- [x] AC2 - Defect-seeded: with `mount` stubbed to return 0 WITHOUT mounting (the real nofail-skip
      mode), the sequence aborts. Removing the assertion must make that test RED.
- [x] AC3 - The failure is distinguishable from a genuine mount error: a reader can tell "the
      volume did not mount" from "mount reported an error", since nofail makes the former silent.
- [x] AC4 - A running-host check exists that an operator can invoke after a stop/start to confirm
      both volumes are mounted where expected, without reading the script. Portable: no dependence
      on a specific CI provider or on AWS APIs.

## Non-goals

Not removing `nofail` from either fstab entry — `nofail` is deliberate, so a missing volume does
not wedge boot. The fix is to ASSERT after mounting, not to make boot fragile.
